flags.why: This interjection is also common in Northern speech and is not restricted to Central and Southern Vietnamese ([dictionary](https://vdict.com/úi,3,0,0.html)).
The entry omits the common use for wavering resolve, confidence or beliefs.
flags.fix: to waver; to become unsettled (of resolve, confidence or beliefs); ex: Tôi bắt đầu lung lay quyết tâm. = My resolve is beginning to waver.

flags.why: This expression for today is used mainly in Southern and Central Vietnamese.

Sắc sảo means sharp or perceptive, not morally upright, which is expressed by ngay thẳng in the example ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/sắc_sảo)).
The entry omits the everyday meaning of forwarding a message or email.
flags.fix: to forward (a message or email); ex: Tôi chuyển tiếp email này cho bạn. = I'll forward this email to you.

flags.why: Tía addresses one's father and is not a general respectful pronoun for an older man.
Applied to a man as in this example, ẻo lả disparages his perceived weakness or femininity.
Thiêng means sacred or spiritually powerful, not simply precious ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/thiêng)).
The entry omits the everyday modern measurement of ten centimetres ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/tấc)).
flags.fix: decimetre; ten centimetres; ex: Tấm ván này rộng hai tấc. = This plank is twenty centimetres wide.

flags.why: The approximately four-centimetre unit is historical and needs a warning distinguishing it from modern usage ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/tấc)).
